screening_decisions.reason: This is an RCT evaluating a nurse-led Minimal Psychological Intervention (MPI) based on CBT principles in COPD patients aged 60+. The study compares MPI with usual care and measures anxiety outcomes using validated scales (SCL). The population meets age criteria (>40), has COPD, and anxiety was assessed. The intervention is a psychological therapy.

This is a cross-sectional observational study using PCA to identify anxiety symptom clusters. It does not test any psychological therapy intervention and is not an RCT. The study aims to understand anxiety patterns, not evaluate treatment effects.

This is a theoretical/conceptual paper about psychiatric training frameworks. It does not involve COPD patients, does not test any intervention, and is not an RCT. Completely outside the scope of the review.
This paper discusses psychophysical methods for measuring effort ratings. It is not about COPD, anxiety, or psychological therapies. Not an RCT and completely unrelated to the review topic.

This is an RCT testing progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) training, which is a psychological/relaxation therapy, in patients with chronic breathing disorders including COPD. The study compares PMR added to standard PR versus standard PR alone. However, uncertainty exists about whether all participants had confirmed COPD (some may have other breathing disorders) and whether anxiety was diagnosed per criteria. Including conservatively pending full-text review.

This is a case-control study investigating brain monoamine transporter density in personality disorder patients. It does not involve COPD patients, is not an RCT, and does not test psychological therapies for anxiety.

While this is an RCT in COPD patients, the intervention is acupressure, which is a physical/complementary therapy, not a psychological therapy. The review specifically seeks psychological therapies for anxiety treatment.
This is a narrative review article summarizing existing literature on anxiety in COPD. It is not an RCT and does not present primary data from an intervention trial.
This is a cross-sectional observational study assessing prevalence of anxiety and depression in COPD patients. It does not test any intervention and is not an RCT.

This is an RCT in COPD patients, but the interventions are exercise training, activity training, and lectures - these are physical/educational interventions, not psychological therapies specifically designed to treat anxiety disorders.
This is a guidelines document from GOLD. It is not an RCT and does not test any intervention. It provides consensus recommendations for COPD management.
This is a prospective cross-sectional study examining risk factors for anxiety and depression in COPD patients. It does not test any intervention and is not an RCT.
This study evaluates fluoxetine (an antidepressant medication), which is a pharmacological intervention, not a psychological therapy. The review specifically excludes medication-only treatments.

This is an RCT (described in Portuguese as 'ensaio clínico prospectivo, controlado e cego') testing psychotherapy as part of a pulmonary rehabilitation program in COPD patients. Three groups were compared: complete PR with psychotherapy, PR without exercise, and PR without psychotherapy. Anxiety and depression were measured using Beck inventories. The study directly tests psychological therapy effects in COPD patients.
This is a methodological paper describing a questionnaire instrument for measuring health status in airways disease. It is not an RCT and does not test any intervention.

This is an observational analysis examining associations between anxiety/depression and COPD symptoms. While it references the INSPIRE-II trial, this specific study analyzes correlations rather than testing an intervention. Not an RCT testing psychological therapy.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques. It is not an RCT, not about COPD, and not about psychological therapies for anxiety.
This is a study protocol describing a planned RCT, not a completed study with results. Protocols do not provide outcome data needed for systematic review synthesis.

This is a Cochrane review focusing on pharmacological interventions for anxiety in COPD. The review explicitly excludes medication-only treatments, and this is a secondary source (review) rather than a primary RCT.

This is an observational factorial design study comparing HRV responses between COPD and healthy controls with varying anxiety levels. It does not test any psychological therapy intervention and is not an RCT.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary randomised controlled trial. The selection criteria require RCTs, cluster-randomised trials, or cross-over trials as the study design.

This is an educational statistics note about units of analysis in clinical studies. It is not a clinical trial, does not involve COPD patients, and does not evaluate any psychological therapy for anxiety.

This is a qualitative study using in-depth interviews with 14 COPD patients. It does not meet the required study design (RCT, cluster-randomised, or cross-over trial) and does not evaluate a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a report of proceedings from a multidisciplinary workshop. It is not a primary research study or RCT, and does not evaluate psychological therapy interventions.

This is a cross-sectional observational study examining relationships between functional status, anxiety, depression, and COPD severity. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any psychological therapy intervention.
This is a review article discussing theoretical perspectives on panic disorder in COPD and the potential utility of CBT. It is not a primary RCT evaluating a psychological therapy intervention.

This is an RCT evaluating cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for anxiety and depression in COPD outpatients. CBT is a psychological therapy, anxiety was measured using the Beck Anxiety Inventory (validated scale), and the comparison was enhanced standard care. While the comparison group received 'enhanced standard care' rather than strictly 'no intervention or education only', this is a reasonable control condition and the study warrants full-text review to assess eligibility.
This is a systematic review examining psychological interventions for anxiety in COPD. It is not a primary RCT. While it reviews RCTs, the review itself does not meet the study design criteria.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal observational studies examining associations between depression/anxiety and COPD outcomes. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate psychological therapy interventions.
This is a cross-sectional survey study examining the relationship between social support and anxiety in COPD patients. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any psychological therapy intervention.

This is a methodological paper providing empirical estimates of intracluster correlation coefficients for sample size calculations in cluster-randomised trials. It is not a clinical trial evaluating psychological therapy for anxiety in COPD.

This is an RCT evaluating a telephone-based coping skills training (CST) intervention, which is a psychological therapy, in COPD outpatients aged 38-81 years. Anxiety was measured as an outcome. The comparison group received COPD education only, which meets the criteria for 'education only' comparison. The study meets all key selection criteria.

This is a review/commentary article discussing the relationship between depression and COPD, summarizing evidence from various trials, and outlining a research agenda. It is not a primary RCT evaluating psychological therapy for anxiety in COPD.

This is an RCT evaluating cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for preventing panic attacks and anxiety symptoms in COPD patients who had undergone pulmonary rehabilitation. CBT is a psychological therapy, anxiety outcomes were measured, and the comparison was routine care. While routine care may not be strictly 'no intervention or education only', this warrants full-text review to determine if the control condition meets criteria.

This is a prospective observational cohort study examining risk factors for rehospitalisation in COPD patients, including anxiety as a predictor. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any psychological therapy intervention.

This is an RCT evaluating relaxation therapy (a psychological intervention) for reducing anxiety and dyspnea in COPD patients. The comparison group was instructed to sit quietly (essentially no intervention), which meets the criteria. Anxiety was measured as an outcome. The study meets key selection criteria, though age details are limited to 'adult COPD patients'.

This is an observational cohort study examining the relationship between anxiety and health outcomes in COPD patients from the FLOW cohort. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate any psychological therapy intervention.
This is a review article providing an overview of the burden and management of depression and anxiety in COPD. It is not a primary RCT evaluating psychological therapy interventions.
This is a commentary/educational article discussing anxiety in COPD patients. It is not a primary research study or RCT, and does not evaluate any psychological therapy intervention.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating psychological and lifestyle interventions for depression and anxiety in COPD. While it reviews relevant RCTs, the review itself is not a primary RCT and does not meet the study design criteria.

This is a correlational/path analysis study examining variables influencing functional status in COPD. It is NOT a randomised controlled trial and does not test any psychological therapy intervention.

RCT comparing CBT group treatment for anxiety/depression with COPD education in COPD patients with moderate-to-severe anxiety/depressive symptoms. Uses validated measures (BAI, BDI-II). Comparison is education only. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT assessing psychotherapy effect on anxiety/depression in COPD patients (mean age 60.33y). Experimental group received psychotherapy plus exercise/physiotherapy; control received exercise/physiotherapy alone (co-intervention matched). Uses validated measures (BAI, BDI). Meets selection criteria including co-intervention requirement.
This study reports community norms for anxiety questionnaires (BAI, FQ, PSWQ, SPAI). It is NOT an RCT and does not test any intervention.

RCT of stress management program, but population includes both obstructive AND restrictive pulmonary disease (not COPD-specific). Abstract does not confirm participants had diagnosed anxiety disorders or used validated anxiety scales. Does not clearly meet population criteria.
This is a review/discussion article about pathophysiologic relationships among dyspnea, hyperventilation, and panic anxiety. It is NOT an RCT and does not test any intervention.

Cross-sectional study revising and validating the COPD Anxiety Questionnaire (CAF-R). Examines association between COPD-related fears and disability. NOT an RCT and does not test any psychological therapy intervention.
Describes development/validation of Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. NOT an RCT and does not test any intervention.

RCT comparing comprehensive pulmonary rehabilitation (exercise, education, psychosocial support) with education alone. While psychosocial support was included, the PRIMARY intervention is physical rehabilitation/exercise training, not psychological therapy. Depression measures showed no significant difference between groups. Does not meet intervention criteria.
Literature review on anxiety and depression in COPD patients. NOT an RCT and does not test any intervention.
Study comparing different duration walking tests for exercise tolerance assessment. NOT an RCT and does not test any psychological therapy intervention.
Theoretical/review article discussing connections between panic disorder and respiratory physiology. NOT an RCT and does not test any intervention.
Small observational study (n=16) examining correlates of daily impairment in severe COPD. NOT an RCT and does not test any psychological therapy intervention.
Prevalence study and validation of BASDEC screening questionnaire in elderly COPD patients. NOT an RCT and does not test any psychological therapy intervention.
Systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating psychological interventions in COPD. NOT a primary RCT.
Critical review of literature on association between psychological distress and COPD exacerbations. NOT an RCT and does not test any intervention.
Review article on epidemiology, comorbidity, diagnosis, and treatment of anxiety in pulmonary disease. NOT an RCT and does not test any intervention.

Single-blind RCT comparing one 2-hour CBT session (with relaxation training, cognitive interventions, graduated practice) with COPD education in elderly COPD patients. Uses validated measures (BAI, Geriatric Depression Scale). Comparison is education only. Meets all selection criteria.
